findings.title: totalPages uses floor+1, producing a phantom empty last page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members with limit 50) this returns 3 instead of 2, so `showingLast` never becomes true for the real last page, the pager shows "2/3", and clicking next sets `offset` to `user_count` (see `next`, which clamps with `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), causing `findMembers` to request an offset equal to the total and render an empty member list. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no bounds. A request with `?limit=1000000` to this unauthenticated endpoint will serialize an arbitrary number of users (expensive JSON + N queries for avatars etc.), and a negative value such as `?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` makes PostgreSQL raise "OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative", returning a 500. Clamp limit to a sane maximum and force offset to be non-negative.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses GroupUser callbacks and 404s for non-members
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` operates on a `has_many :through` association, whose default deletion strategy is `delete_all`: the join row is removed with raw SQL, so `GroupUser`'s `counter_cache` on `user_count` and its `after_destroy` hooks (clearing the user's primary group / granted title) never run. The result is a stale `Group#user_count` and users keeping a primary group/title from a group they no longer belong to. The previous code path used `group.remove(user)` / destroyed the `GroupUser` record, which ran those callbacks. Additionally, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an integer id calls `find` on the scoped association, so removing a user who is not a member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (404 instead of a JSON error). Use `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all` (or `group.remove(user)`).

findings.title: PATCH /admin/groups/:id now silently hides groups and drops 'changes'
findings.body: The `update_patch` branch was removed, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH to `update`. Any existing client (plugin, script, or a browser still running the old JS during a deploy) that sends `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `{changes: {add: ...}}` now hits the new `update`, which ignores `changes` entirely, sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` (i.e. false because `visible` is absent) and responds with `success_json`. Membership changes are silently lost and the group is silently made invisible. The same unconditional `visible` assignment makes every partial update (any PUT without an explicit `visible`) flip the group to hidden; it should only be assigned when the parameter is present.

findings.title: create silently drops alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) includes `alias_level`, and admin/templates/group.hbs renders the alias-level combo box for a brand-new group, but `create` only reads `name` and `visible`. An admin who picks an alias level while creating a group gets a group with the default alias level and no indication that the setting was ignored; they must save a second time. Read `params[:alias_level]` in `create` as `update` does.

findings.title: Members endpoint response shape changed without spec coverage
findings.body: `GET /groups/:group_id/members` previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users; it now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and is paginated (default 50) for all groups, not just automatic ones. This is a breaking change for any external consumer/plugin reading the array form and for non-automatic groups that previously received every member. No spec was added or updated for the new payload or for the pagination behaviour (`spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` is untouched in this PR), so neither the contract change nor the limit/offset handling is tested.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise for unnamed groups
findings.body: `findMembers` now does `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` where it previously returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Any caller that chains (`group.findMembers().then(...)`) will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined` for a group without a name (e.g. an unsaved new group). Keep returning a resolved promise so the method's contract stays uniform.

findings.title: No error feedback when adding/removing members fails
findings.body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` call into the model and ignore the returned promise's rejection. The server can legitimately fail these calls (422 `can_not_modify_automatic`, `render_json_error(group)`), and `add_members` silently skips usernames that don't resolve to a user. In all those cases the UI just re-renders the unchanged list with no message, and the rejected promise surfaces only as an unhandled rejection in the console. Add a failure handler that shows the server error (as the `save` action does).

findings.title: destroy() returns undefined for unsaved groups while caller chains .then()
findings.body: `destroy` returns `undefined` when the group has no `id`, but admin-group.js.es6's `destroy` action does `group.destroy().then(...)`. admin/templates/group.hbs renders the Delete button for every non-automatic group, including the unsaved new-group form, so clicking Delete before saving throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined` and leaves `disableSave` stuck at true. Either return a resolved/rejected promise or hide the button when `id` is absent (the members section already uses `{{#if id}}`).

findings.title: remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and a hardcoded group id
findings.body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but config/routes.rb only exposes `remove_member` via DELETE. Controller specs don't verify the verb, so this test passes while never exercising the route the client actually uses, and a future routing mistake on the DELETE path would go unnoticed. It also assumes the seeded group with `id: 1` is automatic (same for the add_members and update examples); fabricating an automatic group would make the expectation explicit and robust.

findings.title: Rename path does not strip whitespace like create does
findings.body: `create` does `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip` (and there is a spec for it), but `update` assigns `params[:name]` verbatim. Renaming a group to " bob " therefore stores the untrimmed name, producing group names that no longer match the username-style rule enforced at creation time and that will not match lookups such as `Group.find_by("lower(name) = ?", name.downcase)` for the trimmed value. Strip the name in `update` as well.
